items.headline: OpenAI Launches GPT-6.1 Sol at DevDay
items.summary: OpenAI introduced GPT-6.1 Sol, a cheaper, faster model priced at one-fifth of GPT-6 Astra that the company says delivers near-Astra performance for agentic coding, computer use, and professional work. It also improves factual accuracy, cutting the error rate on difficult prompts from 11.4% to 7.7% versus GPT-6 Sol.

items.headline: Google Begins Rollout of Gemini 4 Argon With 1-Million-Token Output
items.summary: Google started rolling out Gemini 4 Argon, its new flagship model built for long, complex software engineering, finance, legal, and cybersecurity tasks, supporting up to one million tokens in a single response. Access began with trusted partners in Google's cybersecurity-focused Fairwind program ahead of broader API and Ultra availability.

items.headline: Meta's Muse Spark AI Co-Authors Six Math Papers, Five Solving Open Problems
items.summary: Meta said its Muse Spark 1.1 and 1.2 models, used through its ordinary chat interface without a custom research scaffold, helped mathematicians crack six research-level problems spanning probability, differential equations, group theory, and more. Five of the six papers resolve questions that were previously open in their fields, though Meta frames the contributions as bounded, human-directed assistance rather than autonomous discovery.

items.headline: OpenAI Safety Transparency Lead David Robinson Resigns, Says Culture Is 'Broken'
items.summary: Robinson, who spent three and a half years at OpenAI leading safety reports for a dozen major launches, resigned and published an essay arguing the company's iterative-deployment approach guarantees periodic failures that grow more severe as systems become more capable. His departure follows the firing of three other safety staffers days earlier.

items.headline: OpenAI Cuts Ties With Three Safety Researchers Over Alleged Leak
items.summary: OpenAI parted ways with three members of its safety team after they allegedly shared confidential company information with an outside AI safety organization, according to a Wall Street Journal report. The move adds to a turbulent week for OpenAI's safety organization amid broader scrutiny of how the company manages risk disclosures.

items.headline: Anthropic's Mythos AI Finds Critical File-Server Flaw, Exploited Within a Day
items.summary: Anthropic's bug-hunting model Mythos identified CVE-2026-61500, an authentication-bypass flaw in Rejetto HTTP File Server caused by a reversible pseudo-random session-key generator, by chaining two separately-identified weaknesses into a working exploit path. Attackers began exploiting vulnerable servers within a day of disclosure, underscoring how AI is compressing the window between vulnerability discovery and real-world exploitation.

items.headline: Nvidia Launches 64GB DGX Spark at $4,999 for Local AI Development
items.summary: Nvidia introduced a lower-memory 64GB variant of its DGX Spark desktop AI computer, priced at $4,999 and built on the same GB10 Grace Blackwell superchip as the 128GB model, to make local fine-tuning and agentic development more affordable. The system can run models with up to 100 billion parameters and ships through OEM partners including Dell, HP, and Asus starting October 23.

items.headline: Nvidia Faces Scrutiny Over AI Chip Smuggling to China
items.summary: Bloomberg reports Nvidia is facing questions from officials about why it missed red flags as its AI chips continued reaching China despite US export curbs, highlighting ongoing tension between the chipmaker's growth and regulatory enforcement.

items.headline: xAI Releases Grok 4.7 With New Flagship Model
items.summary: xAI rolled out Grok 4.7, adding a new flagship model and a refreshed AI encyclopedia feature, and made it available through its Ramp Router model-routing platform with a limited-time discount for early adopters.

items.headline: Arizona Appeals Court Vacates Manslaughter Sentence Over AI 'Victim' Video
items.summary: The Arizona Court of Appeals ordered a resentencing for a man convicted in a road-rage shooting after ruling that an AI-generated video depicting the deceased victim forgiving his killer improperly swayed the sentencing judge, who had called the video 'genuine.' The ruling is among the first in a US court to find that an AI-generated victim statement can render a sentencing fundamentally unfair.

items.headline: Microsoft's AI-Driven Quarter Adds $1 Trillion in Market Value
items.summary: Microsoft shares jumped 37.5% from July through September, their best quarterly performance since 1998, adding roughly $1 trillion to its market capitalization as investors continued to reward the company's AI infrastructure and Copilot investments.

items.headline: Boston Dynamics Gives Atlas a Four-Fingered Hand Built for Factory Work
items.summary: Boston Dynamics unveiled a new 13-degree-of-freedom, four-finger hand for its Atlas humanoid robot, dropping the pinky in favor of a stronger opposable thumb designed for gripping factory tools. The upgrade comes as Atlas trains at a Hyundai facility near Savannah, Georgia, ahead of a planned 25,000-unit deployment across Hyundai and Kia plants.
